The Index

What the AI Visibility Index Measures

Buyers increasingly open an AI assistant before they open a search results page. When they ask which KYC vendor to use or which treasury platform is best, the engine names a handful of companies. This edition compares the provider's visibility scores for a selected set of fintech and AI brands. Read the date, market and scoring method alongside the results. Our answer engine optimization work also uses a separate client panel with dated answers to specific buyer questions.

The Engines

The July edition uses Semrush AI Visibility data covering ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Perplexity and Gemini. Coverage can differ across engines and markets.

The Questions

This edition uses the questions and topic coverage available in the source dataset. It is separate from our client monitoring panel, where we record a defined set of buyer questions and the dated answers.

The Score

Scores use the source provider’s 0 to 100 visibility scale. In the July sample, 14 was the lowest returned score and four brands fell below tracking. These are observations about this dataset, not a universal scoring threshold.

The Benchmark

Every score sits beside its category best: the strongest sources answering those same questions today. In most categories that is a review site, a bank or a publisher rather than a vendor.

An AI brand index, or brand visibility index, compares a defined sample at a recorded time. The July results cannot establish conversion impact or predict the next answer a buyer sees. Geography, question selection and provider coverage can change the result. Our monthly client answer panel is a separate measurement and should be compared on its own terms.

July 2026 Edition

Nobody Owns AI Search Yet

We scored 63 B2B brands (this edition's category: fintech and AI) on how often each one appears when a buyer asks an AI engine which product to use. The category average came back at 22 out of 100. One brand has claimed its answer. Everyone else is still available.

22/100Average score across the 63 brands measured
1 of 63Scored above 50
19Median score out of 100
56 of 59Scored brands sitting below their own category best

One brand in 63 owns its answer.

Wise scores 78 out of 100. The next best, Adyen, sits at 45, and every other brand in the index is under 40. Wise is also the only one of the 63 that outperforms the strongest answer sources in its own category.

Strong US brands go quiet worldwide.

Chime scores 74 in the US and 39 worldwide. Ramp scores 67 against 27, Plaid 64 against 28, Brex 64 against 26. The answer a buyer gets changes with the continent they are asking from, and almost nobody defends both.

Somebody else is answering the buying questions.

56 of the 59 scored brands sit below the strongest answer sources in their own category. Review sites, banks and publishers hold those answers today, which means the vendor is absent from the moment the buyer is deciding.

Whole categories are unclaimed.

Treasury, KYC, WealthTech and RegTech all average in the teens. The first brand to claim one of those categories becomes the default answer inside it, and defaults compound with every answer that gets generated.

The Programme

One Vertical at a Time

The Index is a standing research programme rather than a one-off study. Each edition takes a single category, scores the brands competing inside it, and publishes the shape of the field.

The July 2026 edition covers fintech and AI, a category whose buying questions are unusually well defined, which makes it a clean first measurement. Later editions take other B2B categories. Our fintech and AI engagements draw on the same data.

More verticals follow as editions publish. The question set stays stable between runs, so a score that shifts between editions shifted because the answers shifted. Every edition carries the month it was measured, and any question added to the set gets noted in it.
